This combination of clear licensing and thorough documentation helps maintain both transparency and compliance.

Incorrect

Focus on building a proprietary model without worrying about the data sources used.

Ignoring data sources is risky, as improper use of data can lead to legal issues. It is important to ensure that all data is used according to its licensing terms, whether the model is proprietary or open-source.

Only use models with high accuracy, ignoring transparency and licensing details.

Focusing solely on accuracy without considering transparency and licensing could lead to non-compliance with regulations and a lack of trust from users.

Regularly update the model‘s parameters without documenting the changes

Regular updates are good practice, but without proper documentation, it becomes difficult to ensure transparency, track improvements, or demonstrate compliance with regulations.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/model-cards.html

https://aws.amazon.com/opensource

questions.text: An online video platform wants to implement a feature that auto-generates video summaries to enhance user engagement. Which generative AI technique is the most relevant for this use case?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Summarization models

Summarization models are specialized generative AI techniques designed to condense large volumes of text or spoken content into shorter, coherent summaries while retaining the key information and context. In the context of an online video platform, these models can process the video‘s audio transcripts to extract the most important points and generate concise summaries. This capability enhances user engagement by allowing viewers to quickly understand the essence of a video, helping them decide whether to watch the full content. Summarization models leverage natural language processing (NLP) techniques to understand and interpret the content, making them highly relevant for generating video summaries. By implementing summarization models, the platform can improve user experience, increase content discoverability, and keep users engaged by efficiently delivering information that aligns with their interests.

Incorrect

Image generation models

Image generation models are designed to create new images based on patterns learned from training data. They are used in applications like generating realistic photos, artwork, or enhancing image resolution. While powerful for visual content creation, they are not suitable for generating video summaries, which require processing and summarizing textual or audio information from videos rather than creating new images.

Diffusion models

Diffusion models are a type of generative model primarily used for generating high-quality images through a process of iterative refinement. They excel in tasks like image synthesis and denoising. However, they are not applicable to the task of summarizing video content, as they do not handle the textual or auditory data necessary for generating summaries of video content.

Vector embeddings

Vector embeddings are numerical representations of data (such as words, phrases, or images) in a continuous vector space, capturing semantic relationships between items. They are fundamental in various machine learning tasks, including search, recommendation systems, and as input features for models. While embeddings are crucial for processing and understanding data, they are not generative models capable of producing summaries. They might be used within summarization models but are not the technique that directly generates summaries.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/techniques-for-automatic-summarization-of-documents-using-language-models

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/getting-started.html

questions.text: A company using AWS to build a generative AI application needs to decide between using pre-built models or custom models. While custom models provide flexibility, the company is concerned about cost. What is a key cost-related factor to consider when choosing custom models over pre-trained ones?

options.text: Custom models require significant compute resources for training, increasing cost.
Custom models offer fixed pricing, reducing overall cost.
Custom models automatically reduce operational costs due to better optimization.
Pre-trained models are less scalable, which increases long-term costs.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Custom models require significant compute resources for training, increasing cost.

When you choose to use custom models, one of the major cost-related factors is the significant compute resources needed for training the model. Custom models need large amounts of data and computational power, such as using GPUs or specialized hardware like AWS's EC2 instances, to fine-tune the model. Training these models often takes time and requires ongoing monitoring and optimization, which increases the overall cost. Compared to pre-trained models, which are ready to use out-of-the-box, the custom model path can be much more expensive due to these resource-intensive training needs.

Incorrect

Custom models offer fixed pricing, reducing overall cost.

Custom models do not offer fixed pricing; the costs are based on the resources used for training and deployment. The flexibility and complexity of custom models often result in higher costs.

Pre-trained models are less scalable, which increases long-term costs.

Pre-trained models are highly scalable and can handle increased workloads without significant cost changes, making them cost-effective over time.

Custom models automatically reduce operational costs due to better optimization.

Custom models can be optimized, but they do not automatically reduce operational costs. In fact, they usually increase costs due to training and maintenance needs.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/canvas-build-model.html

questions.text: Your company is implementing a foundation model to process and analyze social media posts in different languages. The model must understand both text and images. What key capability should the foundation model have to support this?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Multi-modal support

For a foundation model to process and analyze social media posts that include both text and images, it must have multi-modal support. Multi-modal models can handle different types of data simultaneously, such as text, images, audio, or video. This capability allows the model to understand and analyze social media posts comprehensively by extracting insights from both text and images. Multi-modal support ensures that the model can process and integrate information from multiple sources to provide accurate and relevant analyses.

Incorrect

In-context learning

In-context learning allows a model to generate responses based on a provided context but does not address the need for handling different data types like images and text.

Few-shot prompting

Few-shot prompting involves giving the model a few examples to help it generalize, but it doesn't relate to the model's ability to process both text and images simultaneously.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

RAG combines retrieval of external information with generation capabilities, which is useful for knowledge-based tasks, but it does not address the need to process both text and images as required in this case.

questions.text: Your company is concerned about potential legal risks with a generative AI system that creates content. What is a major legal risk associated with deploying such systems?

options.text: Lack of response diversity in content generation
High model latency in production environments
Intellectual property infringement due to AI-generated content

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Intellectual property infringement due to AI-generated content

A major legal risk associated with deploying generative AI systems is intellectual property infringement. AI-generated content can inadvertently reproduce or closely resemble copyrighted material, potentially leading to legal challenges. Since the AI model is trained on vast datasets that may include copyrighted works, ensuring that the content it generates doesn‘t violate intellectual property laws is critical. Organizations must take steps to manage this risk, such as implementing filters or using models trained on legally compliant datasets to avoid infringing on third-party rights.

Incorrect

High model latency in production environments

While high latency affects performance and user experience, it is not a legal risk. Legal concerns primarily revolve around content creation and compliance.

Inability to scale the model

Scalability issues are operational challenges, not legal risks. They relate to the model's performance and capacity rather than legal liability.

Lack of response diversity in content generation

While response diversity impacts user experience and content variation, it doesn't pose a legal threat. Legal risks are more concerned with content compliance and intellectual property issues.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/userguide/ml-security-and-intellectual-property.html

questions.text: A malicious actor provides carefully crafted inputs that manipulate your AI system into performing unintended tasks, such as bypassing safety protocols. Which risk associated with prompt engineering does this describe?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Jailbreaking

Jailbreaking refers to the act of manipulating an AI system to bypass its built-in safety protocols, ethical guidelines, or usage policies. Malicious actors achieve this by crafting specific inputs or prompts that trick the model into performing unintended actions or generating disallowed content. For instance, they might phrase requests in a way that the AI interprets as permissible, even though it leads to harmful or unauthorized outputs. This poses a significant risk in prompt engineering because it exploits the AI‘s flexibility in understanding and responding to user inputs. Jailbreaking can result in the disclosure of sensitive information, generation of inappropriate or harmful content, and other security breaches. It‘s crucial for developers to anticipate potential jailbreak attempts and implement robust safeguards, such as stricter input validation and context-aware response filtering, to protect the AI system from such vulnerabilities.

Incorrect

Prompt redundancy

Prompt redundancy involves unnecessary repetition within prompts, which can lead to inefficient processing but doesn‘t relate to malicious manipulation or bypassing safety protocols.

Data bias

Data bias occurs when the training data contains prejudiced information, causing the AI to produce skewed or unfair outputs. It doesn‘t describe the intentional manipulation of the AI through crafted inputs.

Zero-shot learning

Zero-shot learning is the AI‘s ability to perform tasks it wasn‘t explicitly trained on by leveraging its existing knowledge. It doesn‘t pertain to the risk of bypassing safety measures through malicious prompts.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/implementing-advanced-prompt-engineering-with-amazon-bedrock

questions.text: You are designing a prompt for a chatbot that requires the model to reason through multiple steps before arriving at a final answer. Which technique allows you to guide the model through this step-by-step reasoning process?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Chain-of-thought prompting

Chain-of-thought prompting is a technique where you guide the AI model to think through problems step-by-step before giving a final answer. By designing prompts that encourage the model to articulate each stage of its reasoning, you help it handle complex tasks more effectively. This approach is especially useful when you want the model to solve problems that require multiple steps, like math calculations or logical reasoning. By breaking down the problem, the model can provide more accurate and coherent responses. In the context of a chatbot, chain-of-thought prompting allows the AI to explain its thought process to the user, making the interaction more transparent and helpful. This not only improves the quality of the responses but also enhances the user‘s understanding of how the AI arrived at its conclusions.

Incorrect

Few-shot prompting

Few-shot prompting involves providing the model with a few examples within the prompt to demonstrate the desired output. While it helps guide the model‘s responses, it doesn‘t specifically focus on encouraging a step-by-step reasoning process.

Zero-shot prompting

Zero-shot prompting asks the model to perform a task without any examples or prior demonstrations. It relies on the model‘s existing knowledge but doesn‘t guide it through multi-step reasoning.

Negative prompting

Negative prompting instructs the model on what to avoid in its responses. It helps prevent undesired content but doesn‘t assist in guiding the model through step-by-step reasoning.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/prompt-engineering

questions.text: A retail company wants to use generative AI to automate customer service chat responses. They are concerned about providing accurate answers to customer queries, particularly for product recommendations. What would be the main limitation they should consider when choosing a generative AI model for this task?

options.text: Generative AI models may hallucinate and provide inaccurate responses.
Generative AI models are limited to text-based outputs and cannot recommend products.
Generative AI models always provide the same response to the same input.
Generative AI models are incapable of understanding natural language.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Generative AI models may hallucinate and provide inaccurate responses.

Generative AI models, such as large language models (LLMs), can sometimes produce responses that are plausible-sounding but factually incorrect or nonsensicala phenomenon known as “hallucination.“ In the context of customer service and product recommendations, hallucinations can lead to misinformation, customer dissatisfaction, and potential harm to the company‘s reputation. Therefore, the main limitation the retail company should consider is the risk of these models providing inaccurate or misleading information to customers. Mitigating this issue may involve techniques like fine-tuning the model with domain-specific data, implementing retrieval-augmented generation, or incorporating human oversight.

Incorrect

Generative AI models always provide the same response to the same input.

Generative AI models often produce varying responses to the same input due to their probabilistic nature. They use randomness in their decoding processes (e.g., through sampling methods like top-k or nucleus sampling), which allows them to generate diverse and creative outputs. While this variability can be adjusted using parameters like “temperature,“ it is not accurate to say they always provide the same response.

Generative AI models are incapable of understanding natural language.

Generative AI models are specifically designed to process and generate natural language. They are trained on vast amounts of textual data to understand language patterns, grammar, and context. While they don‘t “understand“ language in a human sense, they are highly capable of interpreting natural language inputs and producing coherent and contextually relevant outputs.

Generative AI models are limited to text-based outputs and cannot recommend products.

While generative AI models primarily produce text-based outputs, they can indeed recommend products by generating text that includes product suggestions. By integrating the AI model with a product database or knowledge base, it can provide personalized recommendations based on customer queries. Therefore, it‘s incorrect to say they cannot recommend products.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/publicsector/generative-ai-understand-the-challenges-to-realize-the-opportunities

questions.text: A data science team wants to integrate multiple data sources, perform data cleaning, and automate the transformation of data for machine learning model training. Which AWS service is best suited to achieve this task?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

AWS Glue

AWS Glue is a fully managed ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) service that helps in integrating multiple data sources, cleaning data, and automating data transformations. It is specifically designed for preparing data for analytics and machine learning workloads. AWS Glue supports building ETL workflows that can extract data from various sources, clean and transform the data, and make it available for machine learning model training. With features like AWS Glue DataBrew, it simplifies data preparation tasks, making it highly suited for data science teams needing to automate and scale their data pipelines.

Incorrect

AWS Data Exchange

AWS Data Exchange is a service for subscribing to and using third-party datasets. It does not provide data cleaning or transformation capabilities for internal datasets.

Amazon EC2

Amazon EC2 provides scalable compute power but does not offer built-in tools for data cleaning or ETL tasks. It is more suited for running applications and services.

Amazon Transcribe

Amazon Transcribe is a speech-to-text service. While useful for converting audio into text, it is not designed for integrating data sources or performing ETL tasks.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/what-is-glue.html

questions.text: A retail company is using an AI system to predict customer preferences and recommend products. To increase customer trust and engagement, they want to ensure that customers understand how the recommendations are made. Which of the following strategies aligns with human-centered design principles for explainable AI?

options.text: Present explanations in highly technical language to prove the sophistication of the model.
Use a black-box model and avoid showing any information about how recommendations are generated.
Focus solely on improving prediction accuracy without providing explanations to users.
Allow users to provide feedback and understand how their data influences future recommendations.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Allow users to provide feedback and understand how their data influences future recommendations.

A human-centered design approach to explainable AI involves engaging users by giving them the ability to provide feedback and helping them understand how their data affects the AI‘s recommendations. This fosters trust and enhances user engagement, as customers feel more in control and confident in the AI system. Providing clear, user-friendly explanations about how recommendations are made empowers users and builds transparency, which is essential for trust in recommendation systems.

Incorrect

Focus solely on improving prediction accuracy without providing explanations to users.

While accuracy is important, neglecting explanations makes it difficult for users to understand or trust the recommendations, which reduces engagement and satisfaction.

Use a black-box model and avoid showing any information about how recommendations are generated.

Black-box models lack transparency, making it hard for customers to understand why specific products are recommended. This approach goes against human-centered design principles, which prioritize clarity and user understanding.

Present explanations in highly technical language to prove the sophistication of the model.

Using technical language that is difficult for users to understand defeats the purpose of explainability. The goal is to make explanations simple and relevant to users, not to prove technical sophistication.
